sources.title: Batch 0058 frozen repository source context for self-introduction
Frozen personal-fact boundary research for self-introduction
XHS answer content standard — Behavior and personal-experience boundary

claims.text: All preserved source occurrences ask only for a personal self-introduction; interview-source position and company metadata do not establish the user's own biography or work history.

The current repository does not verify the user's education, employment, project responsibilities, technology usage, quantified results, career goals or disclosure preferences, so those fields cannot be converted into first-person assertions.

Repository policy permits a fact-gathering and organization framework when personal evidence is missing; the candidate therefore remains draft/candidate and keeps all evidence-dependent personal fields unresolved.

The candidate does not assert an employer, education, project, technology stack, responsibility, metric, result, preference or career goal as a user fact and explicitly rejects inferring biography from source interview labels.

A ready/curated behavioral self-introduction still requires verified personal facts plus repository human/real-review approval; independent review of the interim framework does not remove those gates.

findings: The interim framework covers the self-introduction prompt without inventing any user biography.
All personal facts remain unresolved until verified attestation exists, preserving the behavior-answer non-fabrication boundary.
The oral structure is useful as a future evidence-backed answer skeleton but is not a substitute for real STAR/personal evidence.
Formal promotion remains blocked by personal-fact attestation and repository human/real-review policy.
